Zero embeddings do not make GRU padding inert: biases and recurrent gates can change hidden states even when the input is zero. Masking outputs afterward cannot undo that effect. For packed execution, move each left-padded history’s valid items into a right-padded temporary tensor, pack using CPU lengths and `enforce_sorted=False`, run the GRU, unpack, then scatter valid outputs back into their original positions to preserve `log2feats(sequence) → B × L × H`. Handle empty histories separately. [PyTorch GRU](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html), [packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html).

An explicit alternative, derived from the GRU recurrence, is `candidate = cell(x_t, h)` followed by `h = torch.where(valid_t[:, None], candidate, h)`. Apply this to every recurrent layer; emit zero features at padding positions and exclude them from loss. This preserves state across padding and supports the original layout directly, but a Python timestep loop may be slower than packed execution. Final readout must gather the last nonpadding index; for nonempty, strictly left-padded histories this is `L-1`, never `length-1`.

Verify in evaluation mode that adding leading zeros leaves aligned valid features, final features, and candidate scores unchanged within numerical tolerance. Compare batched padded execution against individual unpadded histories, including singleton and empty cases; compare packed and masked implementations with identical weights. Preserve per-position scoring: for features `F[B,L,H]` and candidate IDs `I[B,L,K]`, compute `(F.unsqueeze(-2) * item_emb(I)).sum(-1)`, yielding `B × L × K`. Broadcast shared candidates explicitly, retain any trained projection/bias consistently, and compare vectorized scores against a small loop reference. Use identical architecture and scoring in the checkpoint loader and embedded predictor.
